text: Amino acids can be classified as essential (indispensable) or nonessential (dispensable). Essential amino acids (EAAs) cannot be synthesized adequately to support the body's needs and thus must be provided through the diet. Nonessential amino acids, on the other hand, can be synthesized by the body. Deprivation of even a single EAA impairs the synthesis of virtually all cellular proteins via an inhibition of the initiation phase of mRNA translation (39). Certain amino acids are classified as conditionally essential if they are required in the diet when amino acid use is greater than its rate of synthesis (153). Importantly, all 20 amino acids are necessary for proper cell function and growth. lists the essential, nonessential, and conditionally essential amino acids.
